subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm designing a heavy armored hauler truck with six wheels across three axles, a cab, armored plating, a sealed cargo pod with glowing seals, a roof turret gun, neon strips, antenna, and headlights—keeping it a static model without complex joint rigging.

I'm sketching the texture plan: hazard stripes, a shield-and-lock emblem for the pod, neon "CONVOY 07" signage, a cyan HUD windshield overlay, a rune-ring seal glyph, and a circuit-pattern decal for the side panels, using the builder's helper functions for boxes and painted parts.

Now I'm laying out the geometry in coordinates, placing the chassis box, defining wheel axles with cylinder tires and glowing hub discs, mudguards, and starting the cab section forward of the front axle.

Working out the cab shape by extruding a low-poly wedge profile along the z-axis to create that sloped hood-to-windshield silhouette.

Adding side windows as small dark panels, plus a front bumper box and bull-bar with hazard stripe texture for armored detailing.

Now designing the face of the vehicle: glowing cyan grill slits, angular headlight boxes textured with angry-slit visor SVGs glowing magenta/cyan for an eye-like look. I'm placing a roof turret with hex base, twin barrels with glowing muzzle tips, a light bar strip, antennas with glowing tips, and starting exhaust stacks.

Writing geometry for exhaust stacks...

Now sketching the main cargo pod as an extruded hexagonal capsule shape behind the cab, figuring out its length, width, and height along the chassis.

I'm defining a chamfered octagon outline for the pod's cross-section with beveled edges, then planning its paint scheme: pale steel with lighter top, grimy bottom, and dark seam lines every 0.7m along the z-axis to suggest ribbed panels.

Now I'm positioning darker raised rib bands around the pod by slightly scaling up the same outline and extruding thin bands at several z positions, spacing them so they sit between the side decal panels. I'm also placing a glowing magenta seal glyph on the rear door cap near the pod's back end, and thinking through the gap at the front where it meets the cab.

For the top of the pod I'm adding a glowing amber beacon, hazard hatch, vents, cylindrical seal bolts, and a cyan glow seam running along the top to suggest it's sealed. On the sides I'm planning large glowing emblem decals with a shield/lock icon, "SEALED / CARGO 7-K" text, and a barcode, placed as transparent textured planes facing outward on each side.

Working through the orientation math to make sure the text reads correctly from either side rather than appearing mirrored...

Now shifting to the escort vehicle's armor details: angled side plates with hazard stripes and spare reactive armor tiles on the cab.

I'm also planning the glow effects—neon underglow rods in magenta beneath the chassis, cyan accent strips along the pod base, red rear light boxes with mud flaps and a tow hook, an amber lightbar on the roof, and side mirrors on the cab.

I'm adding steps with yellow handrails, dark wheel arch covers, and a small rear turret with a glowing red sensor eye for a guarded look, plus hazard stripes on the pod hatch. I'm working out wheel geometry so the cylinders sit properly on the ground without clipping, and tallying up the overall vehicle height starting from the cab top.

Checking the chassis and wheel positioning now, making sure the wheel radius and placement relative to chassis width don't cause ugly overlaps with the cab and pod bottoms, adjusting the arch covers to mask any minor clipping.

Still writing paint shaders...

Planning out the remaining textures: visor HUD with grid and reticle, a pod emblem with shield and barcode details, headlight slit, grill slits, rear seal glyph, wheel hub ring, and a side plate number. About eight textures total feels sufficient for the design.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for building parts — a generic box/geometry wrapper, a decal-plane helper for applying textures with optional glow, and making sure cylinder parts for wheels use the right axis orientation.

For the tire itself, I'm going with a dark faceted cylinder for grime, then adding a rim hub, bolts, and a slightly smaller sidewall band cylinder for detail instead of trying to model individual tread lugs.

Now I'm placing the side plane with correct offset and verifying texture mapping, then designing a rooftop turret: a cylinder base, an angled head box, two barrel rods extending forward, and tiny glowing magenta muzzle tips at the ends.

Adding sensor eye and antennas...

Now I'm positioning exhaust stacks on the cab rear wall, checking clearances against the pod front and roof slope so they don't collide, capping them with a glowing orange tip.

For windows I'll keep it simple, reusing the visor texture as a dark glass surface rather than building new assets. The grille goes on the cab's front face between the headlight positions, sized to fit within the profile bounds, and I'm now working out where the headlights should sit without overlapping the grille.

For the headlight eyes, I want a mirrored V-slit design on each side, so I'm generating two separate textures via a function that flips the shape rather than trying to mirror a single plane geometry.

Now I'm placing the front bumper with hazard stripes, adding bull bar rods between the bumper and hood, then working on the rear bumper geometry to match where the chassis and pod end.

Still placing rear details...

Working through rib placement so the bottom one lines up near the wheel top, giving ribs a dark metal color. For the side emblem, I'm positioning it on the pod's side wall between ribs, checking if it's wide enough or gets hidden behind a rib, and nudging it outward/upward so it stays visible.

Still spacing ribs...

Placing the beacon at the pod's top-mid, then adding a rear sensor turret with twin rods and a red eye. I'm also working out neon side strips along the pod's bottom edge, adjusting their offset so the ribs don't occlude them.

I'm adding cyan underglow rods beneath the chassis and blocking out the main chassis box dimensions and z-extent.

Still writing chassis geometry... now placing axle beams at the cab and rear positions, then starting a wheel-building function with tire and rim cylinders for the dual-radius wheel assembly.

I'll keep the tire paint simple with flat dark colors rather than fiddly tread geometry, add mudguards, mirror the rim planes for the opposite side, and place the fuel tank cylinders along the z-axis flanking the chassis.

Then I'm positioning the fuel tanks between the axles with a dark teal color and banding, checking clearance against wheel radius and pod height, before moving on to building mirror arms extending from the cab's side surface.

Now I'm placing the mirror boxes with a faint cyan reflective glow, then adding a roof lightbar positioned relative to the turret base with amber glow and end caps, and finally laying out side armor tile positions on the cab in a grid pattern near the door and number plate area.

I'm adding reactive armor blocks as small boxes spaced along the chassis sides with a lighter color and hazard rim, settling on twelve tiles total, then considering a small cyberpunk-style neon glyph sign on the cab side.

I'll swap unreliable glyphs for a simple latin plate "C-07" instead, and use the rng utility sparingly to vary rivet placement and antenna length rather than overcomplicating the scene. Setting up the imports now for the builder utilities, SVG helpers, and glow kit before writing the actual SVG decal strings.

Writing SVG decals for the hazard stripe pattern, the visor gradient with grid lines and reticle, and the emblem badge border...

Designing more small textures now: eye slits with mirrored flip for left/right, a cyan-magenta grill pattern, a hub disc with bolts and center accent, and an ID plate with "C-07" text and hazard underline.

Setting up the color palette constants and helper functions for building box and cylinder parts...

Working out the wheel hub geometry, positioning rim planes and cylinders so they sit flush against the tire sidewall without clipping. For the cab, I'm extruding a 2D profile along the x-axis with a slight bevel and painting it with the armor color.

Now I'm defining the hood's front profile as a set of (z,y) points, then computing the windshield panel's normal vector so I can offset it slightly outward for a glass insert look, placing it at the midpoint between the two defining corners.

I'm skipping extras like wipers and A-pillar boxes, and now setting up the side cab window as a plane positioned on the angled side wall, between the top profile points, sized roughly 1.0x0.5 near z=2.75-3.0.

Below the window I'm placing a door plate and a row of body tiles along the side, spacing them in steps of about 0.35 units to cover the cab length.

For the front face, I'm working out headlight and grill placement — grill centered low with the headlights above it, checking that the bumper's top edge doesn't overlap the grill's bottom so neither gets hidden.

Now I'm positioning the front bumper plane and considering extras like bull bars or a splitter, but deciding to skip those and instead add simple forward-pointing spike shapes as decorative "ram prongs."

Adding spikes along the bumper, then moving to the turret: a cylindrical base, a boxy angular head with armor, and considering a sloped front panel for extra detail.

Placing antenna tips with glowing spheres, then working through dish placement to avoid overlapping the turret base, nudging coordinates around until the geometry clears.

The dish shape works as a concave cone profile tilted up-back, so I'll add a small support stalk. For the exhaust, I'm placing tall cylindrical stacks with glowing amber caps and dark rings at a few heights for detail.

I'm checking wheel clearances against the stack positions, then adding wheel arch fenders as dark armored boxes positioned to span just above the tire tops for the fender flare look.

For the rear axles I'm placing matching dark mud flap boxes behind each wheel, then adding a rear bumper box near the chassis back edge and small glowing red tail light boxes.

I'm placing ribs along the pod at z values 1.3, -0.2, -2.6, and -4.1, fitting the emblem and hazard plane into the gaps between them, and reusing a plate-generating function to add a "POD-7" unit number plate in the remaining slot.

Now I'm sizing the hazard plane against the hull's flat side wall and bevel, then working out the pod's top face geometry with a chamfered edge, a glowing seam box, and hatch panels, considering whether to add a matching hazard texture on top.

I need an explicit up vector to avoid degeneracy, then I'm placing bolts along the rib tops in magenta glow, adding a beacon with a dark base and amber glow dome near the rear, checking for rib conflicts, and now moving on to the rear turret design.

Placing the turret base near the back rib, adding a small sphere dome with barrel rods extending backward past the pod's end and a red glow eye on the side, then positioning neon strip rods along the lower chamfered edges of the pod running most of its length.

Adding a cyan underglow beneath the chassis and a side skirt, then defining the color palette for armor, pod paint, dark trim, steel, tires, rims, and amber accents. Now I'm writing the pod's paint function, blending a sky-tinted gradient based on surface normal direction.

Still writing paint shader logic...

Adding solid paint stripes...

Still defining pod geometry...

For the coupling between cab and pod, I'm adding a dark connector box plus two glowing rods bridging the gap, then noting the SVG should use monospace font for any text elements before writing it all out compactly.
